bead.title: Advertise real commit_capabilities() for postgres, matching sqlite-relational
bead.description:
PROBLEM
Postgres does not override commit_capabilities(), so it reports CommitCapabilities::default() (all false) even once commit_transition and RecoveryReadPort are implemented (pqueue-30765e65, pqueue-a51d53c7) -- the capability flags would still lie by omission, and Snorri's pre-activation capability check (epic pqueue-2201fd37) would reject a backend that actually works.

PROPOSED FIX
Override commit_capabilities() on the in-scope postgres backend(s) to report the capabilities actually implemented (atomic_transition_commit, vectorized_commit, lease_validation, retained_commit_idempotency, non_work_side_records, authoritative_recovery_reads, delayed_awaits_timers as applicable, DurabilityClass::Atomic, and an honest consistency string), matching sqlite-relational's declared set (crates/pqueue-sqlite/src/relational.rs:5731) unless a specific capability is legitimately not yet true on postgres -- in which case declare it false and note why.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- crates/pqueue-postgres/src/relational.rs (and/or lib.rs per scope decision)

OUT-OF-SCOPE
- Nothing left after this bead closes -- this is the epic's final gate.
bead.acceptance:
1. `rg -n 'atomic_transition_commit: true' crates/pqueue-postgres/src/relational.rs` finds the new override.
2. The shared pqueue-conformance commit-transition scenario's positive path passes against postgres purely by capability detection (no test-specific branching needed) -- i.e. the harness picks the positive path automatically because commit_capabilities() now reports true.
3. `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features` passes.
4. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` pass.
